title: How to change the bundle identifier in Xcode on Mac: a guide for developers
metaTitle: How to Change the Bundle Identifier in Xcode on Mac
description: Learn how to change the bundle identifier in Xcode on Mac with this step-by-step guide. Follow our instructions to update your app settings correctly.

intro: To change the bundle identifier in Xcode on Mac, you must access the Signing and Capabilities tab within your project settings. This process requires you to select your target, update the identifier field, and ensure your provisioning profiles remain valid for the new ID.
tldr: Open your project file in the left navigator.
Select your target in the main editor window.
Navigate to the Signing and Capabilities tab.
Update the Bundle Identifier text field.
Clean your build folder to apply the changes.

blocks.text: The bundle identifier acts as a unique string that identifies your app throughout the Apple ecosystem. It must be unique across the entire App Store. Most developers follow a reverse domain naming convention like com.companyname.appname. This structure helps organize your apps and services in your developer account.
Steps to change the bundle identifier in Xcode
Changing this identifier involves a few specific steps in your project settings. Follow these instructions carefully to avoid build errors or signing issues.

Many developers forget to update dependent targets like extensions or widgets. If your main app identifier changes, your extensions must also reflect this change to maintain the correct prefix. Another common error is failing to update the App ID in the Apple Developer Portal if automatic signing fails. Always check your portal settings after making changes in Xcode.

If you have already uploaded a binary to App Store Connect, you cannot simply change the bundle identifier for that existing app record. You must create a brand new app record in App Store Connect with the new identifier. Plan your identifiers carefully before your first submission to avoid this extra work.

faq.question: Can I change the bundle identifier after submitting to the App Store?
faq.answer: No, once an app is uploaded to App Store Connect, the bundle identifier is locked to that specific app record.

faq.question: Do I need to update my provisioning profiles?
faq.answer: If you use automatic signing, Xcode will attempt to update them for you. If it fails, you must manually update your App IDs in the Apple Developer Portal.

faq.question: Is there a web-based version of Xcode?
faq.answer: No, Xcode is a macOS-only application. You must have a Mac to use it.

task: Change the bundle identifier in Xcode

steps.name: Open Project Settings
steps.text: In the Project navigator on the left, click the blue project icon at the very top.

steps.name: Select Target
steps.text: In the main editor, find the Targets section and select your app target.

steps.name: Navigate to Signing
steps.text: Click the Signing and Capabilities tab in the top menu bar of the editor.

steps.name: Update Identifier
steps.text: Find the Bundle Identifier field, type your new string, and press Return.
steps.tip: Ensure the new identifier matches the reverse-domain format.

steps.name: Clean Build Folder
steps.text: Select Product in the menu, then click Clean Build Folder to finalize.

troubleshooting.fix: Check the Apple Developer Portal to ensure the ID is available and not taken by another team.
Ensure all extension bundle identifiers start with the new main app identifier prefix.
